minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  April 30, 2025

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on April 30, 2025. Chairman
Jacques Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m., followed by the flag salute.

Ramara Rubin announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:
   Commissioner Aletha Metcalf - District 1
   Commissioner Olivia Alvitre - District 2
   Commissioner Phyllis Battle - District 3
   Chairman Jacques Lesure - Commissioner at Large
  Absent:
   Commissioner Perryman-Banks - District 4

City Personnel present were as follows:

   Kerri Arroyo  Acting Library Director
   Ramara Rubin  Secretary

PUBLIC COMMENTS.
  a. Helen Lessick, an Inglewood-based Artist and former Public Arts Consultant,
  delivered a presentation on the public art installations housed at the City of
  Inglewood Public Library. Lessick proposed suggestions for preserving public
  artwork.
  b. June Edmonds, Artist, presented on the piece ‘Inglewood Genesis’, she created
  with students in the Inglewood Public Library, and expressed her commitment to
  preserving the original work. Edmonds, formally requested it be put on record,
  that ‘Inglewood Genesis’ be restored to its original intended location following the
  completion of the renovation.
  c. Michael Massenburg, a visual artist and painter, spoke about his mural,
  ‘Inglewood Stories’, which was commissioned for the library atrium. He discussed
  the piece's historical significance and inspiration, highlighting the involvement of
  community members in its creation.
  d. Mona Lisa Whitaker, visual artist and nonprofit administrator, emphasized her
  longstanding advocacy for public art and offered commentary on the proposed
  plans for public art as part of the library renovation.
  e. Commissioner Battle formally requested it be put on record that all matters of
  public art be referred to and addressed by the Arts Commission.
   Arts Commission

  d. Commissioner Metcalf formally requested that her concerns regarding the
  preservation of and resolution of matters related to the public artwork within the
  library be noted.

MINUTES. Commissioner Alvitre moved, and Commissioner Battle seconded, that the
minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on March 19, 2025, be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Lesure and Battle
Noes: None

VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
  a. Jorge Gómez, Artist and CEO of The Money Studios, and Susie Garcia
  presented the Inglewood Night Market, a public activation presented by
  Councilman Eloy Morales and The City of Inglewood in partnership with
  Fortuna Inglewood, celebrating art, local artists and artisans. They outlined
  event details, including the location, timelines, budget, and requested
  $24,600 in funding for the event.
It was moved by Commissioner Alvitre and seconded by Commissioner Battle that the
Night Market be put on the agenda for the May 21, 2025, meeting. The motion was
carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Lesure, and Battle
Noes: None
  b. Rasta Asaru EL discussed the replacement of the Utility Art Box at the Prairie
  and Century intersection, along with the reinstallation of the artwork, at a
  total cost of $1,500.
It was moved by Chairman Lesure and seconded by Commissioner Alvitre that the
replacement of the artwork for a single utility art box be approved. The motion was
carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Lesure, and Battle
Noes: None
  c. Kerri Arroyo, Acting Library Director, presented on the Inglewood Open
  Studios Mixer and reported on the growth of the Local Artist Roster.
  d. Kerri Arroyo, Acting Library Director, reported on the Renovation
  preparation: Action plans for removal and preservation of Inglewood Public
  Library’s ‘Inglewood Stories’ mural by Michael Massenburg.
   Arts Commission

PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. Joyce, the Acting President of Inglewood Open Studios, announced monthly
  mixers to be held on the third Thursday of the month and exhibition at the City of
  Inglewood Public Library on May 24, showcasing Morningside High School student
  artwork.
  b. Helen Lessick, announced the start of a series of hands-on public art workshops
  beginning on May 30 with the first workshop featuring Rasta Asaru EL. The
  workshops are free and open to the public.
  c. Maritza, co-founder of Asteroid Vinyl Café, made comments in support of the
  Jorge Gómez and Susie Garcia in relation to the Inglewood Night Market.

COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. Commissioner Battle expressed appreciation for the community's presence and
  support, encouraged continued participation in future meetings, and
  advocated for meaningful change.
  b. Chairman Lesure reflected on his positive experience attending Semana de
  Panamá, highlighting the event's cultural significance and community
  engagement.
There being no further business to be presented, Chairman Lesure declared the meeting
adjourned at 8:19 p.m.
